newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt unhurt by jobless rate - poll.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt unhurt by jobless rate - poll.

text.p: The Australian government has maintained a 12 percentage point lead over the Labor Opposition despite a recent rise in the unemployment rate, according to a newspaper opinion poll published on Tuesday.
The Australian's Newspoll found primary support for the Liberal-National coalition remained steady at 49 percent, while support for Labor rose one point to 37 percent.
Australian Prime Minister John Howard's lead as preferred prime minister over Opposition Leader Kim Beazley was virtually unchanged at 52 percent, compared with 24 percent for Beazley.
But 24 percent of those surveyed remained uncommitted.
The newspaper said the poll showed there had been little effect on the government from January's rise in the unemployment rate to 8.8 percent from 8.6 percent in December.
In response to the jump, Howard said last week the government did not expect to lower unemployment until economic growth reached 4.0 to 4.5 percent.
Australian GDP grew at 3.1 percent between the December quarters of 1995 and 1996, and the government has forecast growth of 3.5 percent in the year to June 30, 1997.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,132 voters around the country by telephone last weekend.
